job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today was an intense day at school. During our sports practice, Rohan tripped and scraped his knee badly. I remembered our first aid lesson and immediately applied firm, direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth. When the cloth became soaked with blood, I did not remove it; instead, I placed another clean pad directly over the first one to avoid disturbing the clotting process. Later, we saw a student faint from the heat. We made sure he lay flat on his back with his legs slightly elevated to help blood flow to his brain, and we definitely did not try to force water into his mouth while he was unconscious. We also discussed burns in class. My teacher explained that for a minor burn, we should run cool, room-temperature tap water over the area for at least ten minutes. She warned us never to apply ice, as it can damage the skin tissue further. We also learned that for any deep cut, we should wash it gently with clean water rather than scrubbing it harshly, which could cause more damage. It is so important to know these simple steps, as they can prevent serious complications and help someone recover safely until professional medical help arrives.
response.summary: This diary entry outlines correct first aid procedures for managing bleeding, fainting, and minor burns. It emphasizes the importance of avoiding harmful traditional practices like scrubbing wounds or applying ice to burns.
